subject: humanities
passage: Builders in late antiquity and the Middle Ages often incorporated spolia—columns, carved panels, and other pieces taken from older structures—into new monuments. Scholars once dismissed the practice as a sign of declining craftsmanship, but many now argue that reused pieces were often chosen deliberately, for the prestige of the past they carried. ______ the Arch of Constantine, completed in Rome in 315 CE, displays relief panels originally carved for monuments to Trajan, Hadrian, and Marcus Aurelius, emperors whom later Romans remembered as model rulers.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

explanation.why: The second sentence makes a general claim about many monuments: reused pieces were often chosen for the prestige they carried. The last sentence describes one particular monument whose reused panels came from admired emperors. The transition must introduce a single case that illustrates the general claim.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "However" signals a contrast, but the Arch of Constantine supports the newer view rather than challenging it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Specifically" would introduce a more precise statement of the same claim, but the arch is one instance drawn from a broad practice, not a more exact version of the claim itself. This is the closest near miss.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Accordingly" means "as a result," but the arch was not built because scholars later changed their view of spolia.
explanation.D: Correct. "For example" signals that the arch is one illustration of builders reusing prestigious older pieces.
